_doc: Schedule data. Dates are ISO (YYYY-MM-DD) in America/New_York. Each week has an 'element' label, a 'goal', sessions, an 'assignment', and 'milestones'. Session 'type' is 'session' (integrated lecture-lab) or 'showcase'; 'topics' are lecture topics, 'lab' the hands-on activities, 'program' the showcase program. Material values are URLs or null (null renders as 'Coming soon'). Allowed material keys: slides, notes, recording, instructions, code, notebook.

meetings.when: Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Fridays, about 3 hours each
meetings.range: 12 sessions, January 5–29 (days tentative; times to be set)

meetings.when: Additional supervised lab time as needed

meetings.range: Public, invited audience; larger venue to be confirmed

location: One primary robotics lab for all sessions, to be confirmed.
hoursNote: About 36 scheduled hours across 12 sessions, plus open lab time and four weekly assignments.
provisionalNote: Days are tentative and clock times are not yet set; the split of topics between sessions is provisional. Each session combines 20–40 minutes of lecture and demonstration, 90–120 minutes of guided hands-on work, and time for testing, debugging, and discussion.

weeks.title: Motors, gearboxes, and actuators
weeks.goal: Every student builds an actuator, and the class demonstrates coordinated walking motion using student-built actuators.

sessions.title: Motor fundamentals and actuator architecture
topics: BLDC motors: torque, speed, current, and power
Introduction to the Berkeley Humanoid Lite actuators
lab: Inspect actuator components and explore motor characteristics
Run a Python motor-modeling notebook
Begin individual actuator assembly

sessions.title: Gearboxes, encoders, and feedback control
lab: Complete individual actuator assembly; install prepared electronics and wiring
Inspect mechanical alignment
Calibrate and test actuators; implement basic position control

sessions.title: Actuator control and walking demonstration
topics: Coordinated joint motion and joint synchronization
lab: Finish actuator testing and measure actuator performance
Integrate selected student-built actuators into a prepared BHL-like walking mechanism
Execute coordinated joint trajectories and demonstrate walking motion

assignment.title: Model a motor and plot its torque–speed curve

milestones: One walking demonstration using student-built actuators

weeks.title: Kinematics, dynamics, and humanoid assembly
weeks.goal: Assemble and commission the full Metal2Humanoid, targeting walking by Friday. Remaining walking validation may extend into Week 3.

sessions.title: Robot modeling, kinematics, and assembly
topics: Degrees of freedom and joint configurations
Forward and inverse kinematics; coordinate frames
lab: Explore the robot simulation and URDF
Begin assembly of assigned subsystems: left leg, right leg, left arm, right arm, torso, and system integration
Install actuators, brackets, and links; inspect alignment and joint limits against the CAD

sessions.title: Dynamics, balance, and robot commissioning
topics: Robot dynamics; center of mass and stability
Joint-level feedback control and trajectory generation
lab: Continue mechanical assembly; connect prepared wiring and communication interfaces
Verify joint IDs and configurations; test joints and limbs independently
Perform supported-motion tests and load pretrained controllers

sessions.title: Whole-body integration and walking
topics: Whole-body coordination; balance and locomotion control
lab: Complete humanoid integration; validate joint configurations and communication
Supported standing and walking tests; supervised walking attempts
Record and resolve integration issues

assignment.title: Implement forward and inverse kinematics and basic end-effector motion

milestones: One assembled Metal2Humanoid with subsystem and safety checks complete
Supported standing and walking tests; walking demonstration targeted by the end of the week (validation may continue into Week 3)

weeks.title: Robot learning and skills
weeks.goal: Develop robot skills in simulation and deploy them to the humanoids where feasible. Skills work starts on schedule even if hardware debugging continues.

sessions.title: Reinforcement learning and locomotion
topics: Markov decision processes; reinforcement learning and PPO
lab: Run humanoid locomotion simulations and evaluate pretrained walking policies
Modify rewards and controller parameters; train or fine-tune a policy
Compare simulated and physical performance; continue walking validation if needed

sessions.title: Imitation learning and sim-to-real
lab: Collect or inspect demonstration data; train or adapt a simple imitation-learning policy
Test skills in simulation; deploy selected behaviors to hardware where feasible
Compare learned and programmed behaviors

sessions.title: Robot skills development
topics: Skill interfaces; preconditions and termination conditions
Success and failure detection; execution monitoring
lab: Each team develops a skill, such as balancing, walking to a target, turning, reaching, gestures, simple manipulation, or recovery
Test in simulation and deploy feasible skills to hardware; evaluate reliability
Integrate skills into a shared library and select showcase demonstrations

assignment.title: Train or fine-tune a locomotion policy and evaluate its performance

milestones: Six team-developed skills, with initial deployment to hardware and a shared skill library

weeks.title: Planning, integration, and showcase
weeks.goal: Combine skills into coordinated behaviors and demonstrate the two humanoids at a public event.

sessions.title: Robot skills and task planning
topics: Hierarchical robot control; predicates and abstract states
Skill sequencing and task and motion planning
lab: Implement a basic task planner; define skill preconditions and effects
Sequence multiple skills; test execution and recovery
Connect planners to the shared skill library

sessions.title: Task and motion planning and final integration
topics: Bilevel planning and learned skill integration
lab: Integrate team-developed skills and test complete demonstrations
Validate hardware and software interfaces; complete safety checks
Rehearse presentations and prepare backup demonstrations

sessions.title: Metal2Humanoid public showcase
program: Introduction to Metal2Humanoid and the student-built actuators
Berkeley Humanoid Lite walking and skills demonstration
Six team presentations: contribution, hardware or software developed, live or recorded demonstration, results and lessons learned
Interactive demonstrations where safe; closing discussion and networking
sessions.note: Held in a larger venue with an invited audience. Live demonstrations depend on robot readiness and safety approval; recorded and simulation backups are prepared.

assignment.title: Implement skill sequencing or a simple task-and-motion planner

milestones: Integrated robot skills and planning; six team presentations
